report:
## Report

The best current evidence does **not** support the claim that ivermectin lowers COVID-19 mortality. Early hopeful signals came mostly from small, low-quality, or later-discredited studies (some involving fraud or bias), which fueled advocacy but did not hold up under rigorous testing.

The largest and most methodologically robust trials show no mortality benefit:
- **TOGETHER trial** (Brazil, ~3,500 patients), published in *NEJM*, found ivermectin did not reduce hospitalization or death from COVID-19 compared with placebo (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869).
- **ACTIV-6** (a large U.S. platform RCT) tested standard and higher ivermectin doses in outpatients and found no meaningful improvement in recovery time, hospitalization, or death (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2801827; https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2797483).
- The **Cochrane systematic review**, the highest standard of evidence synthesis, concluded there is no reliable evidence supporting ivermectin for treating or preventing COVID-19, rating certainty of existing data as very low to low (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD015017_ivermectin-preventing-and-treating-covid-19).

Based on this accumulating high-quality evidence, the **World Health Organization** in November 2023 strongly recommended *against* using ivermectin as a COVID-19 treatment, citing lack of evidence and biological implausibility at safe doses (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivermectin_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic). The U.S. FDA has also never authorized ivermectin for COVID-19.

Some early meta-analyses (e.g., Bryant et al. 2021) reported apparent mortality benefits, but subsequent scrutiny found these were driven largely by smaller, lower-quality, or retracted/fraudulent studies; larger and more rigorous trials conducted afterward did not replicate any mortality benefit.

**Conclusion:** Current high-quality evidence (large RCTs and Cochrane meta-analysis) indicates ivermectin does **not** reduce COVID-19 mortality, contradicting the premise that the answer is "yes."
